title: A Devanagari vowel sign is cut away from its consonant
what: clip() keeps multi-part characters whole through its sticks() table, which lists Latin combining marks, emoji joiners, skin tones and tags but no Indic vowel sign. A preview that falls between a consonant and its matra therefore cuts the matra off: clipping an 11-letter prefix followed by U+0915 U+093F to 13 characters returns the bare consonant and an ellipsis, which renders as a dotted circle in the prompt card, the latest-turn preview, a child run's title and the tab name.
expected: The cut backs up before the consonant so the letter and its vowel sign stay whole, as it already does for a letter with a Latin combining accent.

title: A Claude session id held in two project folders is picked arbitrarily
what: find_session_exact's Claude branch walks the project folders and takes the first <id>.jsonl it meets, so when two folders hold the same id (a managed account folder and ~/.claude, or a copied config) it returns whichever read_dir yields first, and the pick can change when the folder set does. plan() then builds the resume line and the working folder from that arbitrary transcript, and find_session hands it on as if it were the one session, though its own doc says an id naming more than one file finds nothing.
expected: An id with more than one transcript is refused with the reason, exactly as the Codex branch of the same function already does.

title: An unanswered WSL check is reported as a stopped distribution
what: without_stopped_wsl asks running_distros() once, and None means wsl.exe could not be run within three seconds. The code folds that None into the same false answer as an empty list, so every WSL root is dropped and the scan report tells the user each distribution 'is not running', a state Kolux never learned, while the function's own doc says None (could not tell) skips them all.
expected: A distribution Kolux could not ask about is named as unknown, not stated to be stopped, so the report says what was actually known.
